refined_question: Let D⊂ℂ² be a domain with real-analytic pseudoconvex boundary, and let p∈∂D be a boundary point of finite type 4. Must D be locally convexifiable near p; that is, do there exist local holomorphic coordinates in a neighborhood of p in which ∂D is convex?
justification: I cannot faithfully identify an exact Conjecture 1.1/Proposition 1.2/Theorem 1.3 inside arXiv:math/9509202, because that identifier currently resolves to The Several Complex Variables Problem List rather than a convexifiability paper. The closest accessible official formulation matching your draft is the type-four local convexifiability question described by Kolář: after noting that type-four weakly pseudoconvex domains in ℂ² are known to admit supporting functions, he states that it is still unknown whether all such domains are locally convexifiable, and then proves an affirmative result under the additional rigidity assumption. Your draft is therefore too broad in one direction (all finite type rather than type 4) and introduces an extra condition in another (continuous boundary values of the biholomorphism) that is not part of the accessible official formulation.
